title: The singing trio and the Rite Spot in Glendale
summary: He describes how his trio copied Nat Cole's style and worked supper clubs as entertaining musicians.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Then I see my own thing here on Black-and-White. 'Red Boogie' and 'By The River St. Marie.' That's when our group sang. I guess we were copying Nat Cole's style.
I had the trio. This was the trio with Leonard Enois and Willard McDaniel, piano.

We all sang 'By The River St. Marie' in unison. But we used to do a lot of singing. I guess we more or less called ourselves entertaining musicians then. Because we'd play in supper clubs and in dining rooms. Like, we worked at the Rite Spot in Glendale. Do you remember the Rite Spot?
A big tall tower and a circle at the top saying 'Rite Spot.'
